# 25. Asset Management

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Control images, fonts, icons, video, documents, and downloads so they are legal, optimized, accessible, and maintainable.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] An asset inventory with owner, source, license, usage rights, alt guidance, file format, dimensions, and expiry or review date where relevant.
- [ ] An image naming convention using descriptive lowercase hyphenated filenames.
- [ ] An image optimization policy covering AVIF, WebP, JPEG, PNG, SVG, dimensions, compression, responsive sources, and lazy loading.
- [ ] A font policy using open-source fonts, system fonts, or self-hosted licensed files.
- [ ] An SVG policy covering sanitization, inline use, accessibility labels, focusability, and external references.
- [ ] A document policy for PDFs and downloads including accessibility, file size, metadata, and versioning.
- [ ] A video and audio policy covering captions, transcripts, poster images, compression, hosting, and consent-aware embeds.
- [ ] A retention rule for unused originals, drafts, exports, and large source files.

## Must Be True
- [ ] All production assets must have clear usage rights.
- [ ] Meaningful images must have alt text or nearby text that provides equivalent information.
- [ ] Decorative images must not create noise for assistive technology.
- [ ] Images must be sized for display needs and must not rely on browser downscaling of huge originals.
- [ ] SVGs must not contain scripts, external references, or unsafe embedded content.
- [ ] Fonts must load efficiently and not expose users to unnecessary third-party requests where privacy matters.
- [ ] Downloads must be named clearly and not surprise users with large files.
- [ ] Asset paths must remain stable or be correctly updated across pages.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check file sizes, dimensions, formats, compression, duplicates, unused assets, and missing dimensions in HTML.
- [ ] Check license files or source links for every third-party asset.
- [ ] Check that logos and icons have appropriate accessible names or are hidden when decorative.
- [ ] Check that PDFs are accessible or accompanied by HTML alternatives.
- [ ] Check that video embeds have static preview fallbacks and do not load heavy third-party code unnecessarily.
- [ ] Check that favicon, touch icon, manifest icons, and social preview images exist.
- [ ] Check that asset URLs in CSS and HTML resolve after deployment.
- [ ] Check that image metadata does not leak private location or client information when relevant.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid unlicensed images, copied icons, pirated fonts, and unclear asset provenance.
- [ ] Avoid shipping raw camera images, massive PNGs, duplicate exports, and design originals in deploy output.
- [ ] Avoid icon fonts when inline SVG or small SVG files are better.
- [ ] Avoid hiding essential text inside images.
- [ ] Avoid autoplay media and heavy embeds for decorative content.
- [ ] Avoid external font loading without privacy and performance review.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] Assets must look sharp, load fast, have rights, and support accessibility.
- [ ] The asset folder must be clean enough that unused files can be identified.
- [ ] Real business photography must be preferred where trust depends on authenticity.
- [ ] Every media choice must justify its performance cost.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use audits to flag large assets, missing image dimensions, missing alt, duplicate filenames, risky SVGs, and external asset domains.
- [ ] Use free/open-source optimizers when a project adds an image pipeline.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Images, videos, fonts, icons, SVGs, documents, downloads, favicons, social preview images, and source/original assets are organized, named, licensed, optimized, accessible, and maintainable.
- [ ] Image QA covers loading, paths, formats, sizes, defined dimensions, retina quality, crop quality, brand fit, topic relevance, alt text, decorative handling, and no missing image icons.
- [ ] Video/media QA covers loading, fallback images, muted autoplay, controls, captions, compression, mobile/browser behavior, embeds, fallback links, privacy, and no layout breakage.
- [ ] Fonts and icons are free/open-source where possible, limited, optimized, consistent, accessible, self-hosted when useful, and not pulled from huge libraries for a few assets.
- [ ] Files do not expose private data, hidden metadata, credentials, source notes, backup archives, or unapproved copyrighted material.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
